// Part "roofs": the eight roofs (plan.md ROOFS). Plot 0's hip is roof.json, laid by runParts right after the shell; the
// other seven are laid here by the roof tool, one per plot, with the chimney stacks and the other plots' wall tops kept.
import { roof } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

// keep boxes as { from, to }: the chimney stacks (y0..20) and anything a part builds above the eave that must stay
const stack = (x0, z0, x1, z1) => ({ from: [x0, 0, z0], to: [x1, 20, z1] });

export function build(g) {
  // plot 1 Alhambra: front-gabled low roof behind the shaped parapet (ridge along z), red-tile, eaves on the sides only
  roof(g, [18, 13, 29, 21], "gable", { texture: false, fascia: "spruce", soffit: "spruce",
    y: 9, ridgeAxis: "z", pitch: "half", material: "bricks", overhang: { north: 0, south: 1, east: 1, west: 1 },
    keep: [{ from: [18, 9, 13], to: [29, 14, 13] }, stack(26, 22, 28, 23)],
  });

  // plot 2 Vallonia: side-gabled cottage sweeping down over the full-width porch (ridge along x)
  roof(g, [35, 9, 45, 21], "cottage", { texture: false, fascia: "spruce", soffit: "spruce",
    y: 5, ridgeAxis: "x", material: "spruce_planks", verge: "birch_planks", overhang: 1,
    keep: [stack(33, 16, 34, 18)],
  });

  // plot 3 Puritan: gambrel, ridge along x, steep lower course, shallow upper, long front shed dormer
  roof(g, [51, 13, 61, 21], "gambrel", { texture: false, fascia: "spruce", soffit: "spruce",
    y: 5, ridgeAxis: "x", pitch: 2, upperPitch: "half", lower: 2, material: "deepslate_tiles", verge: "dark_oak_planks", overhang: 1,
    steep: true, dormers: { face: "north", style: "shed", width: 7, count: 1 },
    keep: [stack(49, 16, 50, 18), { from: [51, 5, 13], to: [51, 10, 21] }, { from: [61, 5, 13], to: [61, 10, 21] }],
  });

  // plot 4 Cornell: low hip, wide eaves, hipped dormer on the front, and the hip porch roof over the full-width porch
  roof(g, [67, 13, 77, 21], "hip", { texture: false, fascia: "spruce", soffit: "spruce",
    y: 9, pitch: 45, material: "deepslate_tiles", overhang: 2,
    dormers: { face: "north", style: "hip", count: 1, width: 5 },
    keep: [stack(78, 16, 79, 18)],
  });
  roof(g, [67, 9, 77, 12], "hip", { texture: false, fascia: "spruce", soffit: "spruce",
    y: 5, pitch: "half", material: "deepslate_tiles", overhang: 1,
    keep: [{ from: [67, 5, 13], to: [77, 8, 13] }],
  });

  // plot 5 Stanford: steep side gable with two gabled dormers on the front
  roof(g, [83, 14, 93, 21], "cottage", { texture: false, fascia: "spruce", soffit: "spruce",
    y: 7, ridgeAxis: "x", pitch: 45, material: "deepslate_tiles", verge: "smooth_quartz", overhang: 1,
    dormers: { face: "north", count: 2, style: "gable", width: 3 },
    keep: [stack(87, 17, 89, 19)],
  });

  // plot 6 Winona: front gable, ridge along z at x 104 (gable end to the street)
  roof(g, [100, 13, 108, 22], "gable", { texture: false, fascia: "spruce", soffit: "spruce",
    y: 5, ridgeAxis: "z", pitch: 45, material: "spruce_planks", verge: "birch_planks", overhang: 1,
    keep: [stack(109, 17, 110, 19)],
  });

  // plot 7 Craftsman: front gable with wide eaves and a half pitch, dark slate; the porch roof is a shed low to the north
  roof(g, [114, 13, 125, 21], "gable", { texture: false, fascia: "spruce", soffit: "spruce",
    y: 9, ridgeAxis: "z", pitch: "half", material: "deepslate_tiles", verge: "dark_oak_planks", overhang: 2,
    keep: [stack(126, 16, 127, 18)],
  });
  roof(g, [114, 9, 125, 12], "shed", { texture: false, fascia: "spruce", soffit: "spruce",
    y: 5, pitch: "half", material: "deepslate_tiles", overhang: 1,
    keep: [{ from: [114, 5, 13], to: [125, 8, 13] }],
  });
}

input.summary:
roofs part now builds with 0 REFUSED and 0 off-palette (2084 cells placed); make.sh exits 0 and writes build.nbt.
Fix was in parts/roofs.mjs only: keep boxes on the plot 5 side-gable walls (x 83 and 93), the plot 6 front and back gable triangles (z 13 and 22), and the plot 7 front and back gable triangles (z 13 and 21), so the roof stops overwriting the shell's wall infill.
Trade-off: those gable-end cells now show the wall material instead of the roof's verge trim. The verge reads as wall, not as a trim line.
left: Other parts still refuse writes into earlier parts and are not in scope here: porches (23 refused, e.g. 35,5,9 stripped_spruce_log over lime_terracotta), glazing (230), chimneys (10), and several room parts (P3, P5, P7). make.sh reports them, but they belong to those parts' owners.

Verge trim is missing on the gable-end cells kept for the shell (plots 5, 6, 7). If the plan wants the trim line there, the shell's gable infill has to give way to the roof, and that is a shell-part change.

waste.what: Finding every refused cell. The part report keeps only the first 8 of 83 refusals, so I rebuilt four times to see the next group (calcite gables at x 83/93, then sandstone at z 13/22, then spruce gables at z 13/21).
waste.cost: 4 full make.sh runs, about 1 minute each, plus reading parts-report.json
waste.tool: mcd roof --dry-run or a parts-report option that lists every refused cell grouped by plane and block pair, with a suggested keep box for each group.

waste.what: Choosing keep boxes by hand from the gable walls in shell-east and shell-west, and guessing the y-range each wall owns.
waste.cost: Reading shell source plus three trial builds to check the refusal count
waste.tool: A roof dry-run that reports which of its planned cells already hold an earlier part's block, returned as ready keep boxes.

companions.task: Decide whether the verge trim should survive on the gable ends, where the shell's wall infill now shows, or whether the wall should give way to the roof.

structured_output.summary:
roofs part now builds with 0 REFUSED and 0 off-palette (2084 cells placed); make.sh exits 0 and writes build.nbt.
Fix was in parts/roofs.mjs only: keep boxes on the plot 5 side-gable walls (x 83 and 93), the plot 6 front and back gable triangles (z 13 and 22), and the plot 7 front and back gable triangles (z 13 and 21), so the roof stops overwriting the shell's wall infill.
Trade-off: those gable-end cells now show the wall material instead of the roof's verge trim. The verge reads as wall, not as a trim line.
left: Other parts still refuse writes into earlier parts and are not in scope here: porches (23 refused, e.g. 35,5,9 stripped_spruce_log over lime_terracotta), glazing (230), chimneys (10), and several room parts (P3, P5, P7). make.sh reports them, but they belong to those parts' owners.

Verge trim is missing on the gable-end cells kept for the shell (plots 5, 6, 7). If the plan wants the trim line there, the shell's gable infill has to give way to the roof, and that is a shell-part change.

waste.what: Finding every refused cell. The part report keeps only the first 8 of 83 refusals, so I rebuilt four times to see the next group (calcite gables at x 83/93, then sandstone at z 13/22, then spruce gables at z 13/21).
waste.cost: 4 full make.sh runs, about 1 minute each, plus reading parts-report.json
waste.tool: mcd roof --dry-run or a parts-report option that lists every refused cell grouped by plane and block pair, with a suggested keep box for each group.

waste.what: Choosing keep boxes by hand from the gable walls in shell-east and shell-west, and guessing the y-range each wall owns.
waste.cost: Reading shell source plus three trial builds to check the refusal count
